key_insight: A deep learning surrogate can replace repeated crystal plasticity finite element simulations to optimize polycrystalline microstructures while balancing competing spall and yield strength targets.
engineering_relevance: This enables practical microstructure design under realistic quasi-static and dynamic loading by cutting optimization cost by about four orders of magnitude while retaining full-field physics fidelity.
method: 3D U-Net maps stochastic polycrystalline copper microstructures directly to full-field velocity histories from plate-impact simulations.
Couples the surrogate with stochastic microstructure generation and derivative-free optimization to search the design space efficiently.
Uses a distribution-consistent reliability region (DCRR) based on maximum mean discrepancy to flag surrogate extrapolation during optimization.
evidence_signal: Across multiple optimization cases, CPFE validation showed less than 3% prediction error, with cumulative evaluation time reduced by roughly four orders of magnitude versus direct CPFE optimization.
watch_item: Reliability depends on staying within the surrogate's distribution-consistent region; designs far from the training data may require re-validation with high-fidelity simulation.
paper_title: Deep learning driven framework for optimization of polycrystalline microstructures under competing strength requirements
